brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: Four base pieces in a row, each with a third-depth bin, soil and a plant.

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases feeding every cell
requirements.evidence: One irrigation-mode run (run-1) goes straight through all four bases. The configurator accepted it. I can't check actual water flow or tightness.
A bent four-cell cluster was refused because the run could not turn corners, so I used a straight line.
The configurator doesn't model materials or sealing.

finish.summary: I built a straight row of four bases, each with a bin, soil and a plant. A single irrigation run passes through all four. I added joint bolts and end caps on the open faces. check_build reports no issues and the meshes are clear. A bent layout was refused because the run couldn't turn corners, so the planter is a straight line. Whether the pipe is watertight or the material suits water is not checked.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
